司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not Minister of Works (司空); 建安王休仁 is Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, not "Prince Jian'an Xiu Ren".

Wang Qian of Langya, magistrate of Shanyin, had amassed ill-gotten goods everywhere; at the news of Ge's arrival he resigned of his own accord.
琅邪王騫 is Wang Qian of Langya (surname Wang), not "Prince Qian of Langya".
Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian, "Ge truly fills his post."
Document Controller Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian, "Ge truly fills his post."
典簽 is a Document Controller, not a "Chief Clerk" (長史 is translated chief clerk elsewhere).

In the Tianjia era, he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and, with Director of the Secretariat Liu Shizhi, was envoy to Qi, composing the Record of Routes on the Northern Expedition in three scrolls.

In the Tianjia era he concurrently served as Regular Attendant and, with Gentleman of the Secretariat Liu Shizhi, went as envoy to Qi, composing the Record of the Route of the Northern Journey in three scrolls.
中書郎 is Gentleman of the Secretariat, not Director (中書令/監); the literal field has the same error.
He served as Attendant of the Minister of Works.
He held the post of Attendant Gentleman to the Minister over the Masses.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the Minister of Works (司空); 從事中郎 is Attendant Gentleman. The literal field shares the error.
When the emperor ascended the throne, Mian was appointed Director of the Secretariat, then advanced to General Affairs Attendant of the Secretariat, serving in the inner office.
When the emperor ascended the throne, Mian was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, then advanced to Secretariat Drafter for General Affairs, serving in the inner office.
中書侍郎 is Attendant Gentleman (vice director) of the Secretariat, not its Director (中書令); the literal field has the same error.
He also mastered the genealogies of the hundred clans, and all avoided his taboo name.
He also comprehensively mastered the genealogies of the hundred clans, and always avoided the taboo names of others’ forebears.
皆避其諱 means Xu Mian, knowing every clan’s genealogy, avoided their family taboo names in speech; it is not that others avoided his taboo name.
Once, gathering at night with the gatekeeper, a guest named Yu Gao requested the five offices of the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
Once, at a night gathering with his followers, a guest named Yu Gao asked for the post of Five Offices clerk under the Supervisor of the Household.
閘人 is a graphic error for 門人 (his followers), not a gatekeeper; 詹事五官 is the single post of Five Offices clerk under the Supervisor, not five offices.

Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.

Once in the hall the crown prince lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the National University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Cheng, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.
柳憕 is Liu Cheng (憕 read chéng), not Liu Zong; the lecturer is the crown prince, not Xu Mian. The literal field has the same misreading.
After Tongzhi died, Fu Yin, Military Affairs Counselor of Campaign North, replaced him.
After Tongzhi died, Fu Geng, Military Counselor to the General Who Garrisons the North, replaced him.
伏揯 (variant of 伏暅) is Fu Geng, not Fu Yin; 鎮北諮議參軍 is Counselor to the General Who Garrisons the North. The literal field has the same error.
Later Yin again replaced Yan Zhizhi in managing inauspicious rites.
Later Geng again replaced Yan Zhizhi in managing inauspicious rites.
揯 here is Fu Geng (伏揯/伏暅), not "Yin"; the literal field has the same error.
Yin soon moved to another post, and Miao Zhao, Erudite of the Five Classics, managed inauspicious rites.
Geng soon moved to another post, and Miao Zhao, Erudite of the Five Classics, managed inauspicious rites.
揯 here is Fu Geng (伏揯/伏暅), not "Yin"; the literal field has the same error.
Finally, Director of the Secretariat Zhou She and Yu Yuling, two men, were again ordered to take part in knowing the affair.
Finally, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Zhou She and Yu Yuling, two men, were also ordered to take part in the deliberations.
中書侍郎 is Attendant Gentleman (vice director) of the Secretariat, not its Director; the literal field has the same error.
How can Ning Xiaoxuan's capacity be matched—can Emperor Xiaozhang even be mentioned?
How could Emperor Xiaoxuan of Han compare? And Emperor Xiaozhang is not even worth mentioning.

甯 (= 寧) is the rhetorical "how could", not a surname; 孝宣 and 孝章 are Emperors Xuan and Zhang of Han, conveners of the Stone Canal and White Tiger conferences. "Ning Xiaoxuan" is a mistranslation in both fields.
Your servant, with mediocre understanding, wrongly holds this post. Lingering through accumulated years, I am indeed fit for this responsibility.
Your servant, with mediocre understanding, wrongly took charge of this task; lingering over many years, I truly deserve blame for it.
允當斯責 means "I truly deserve the blame" (for the long delay), not "I am indeed fit for this responsibility"; 謬司其任 is a modest "wrongly took charge". The literal field has the same error.
Recently building the two residences of eastern descendants and grandchildren, I relied on the funds from Shizhu's return south. What was needed within was still not small.
Recently, in building two houses for my sons and grandsons on the east side, I relied on the funds Shizhu brought back on returning south; what was needed for them was still considerable.
東邊兒孫二宅 means two houses on the east side for sons and grandsons, not "residences of eastern descendants"; the literal field shares the wording.
Though the matter differs from the mound of sleep, it can briefly be likened.
Though the matter differs from the barren Qinqiu land, it may roughly be compared to it.
寢丘 is Qinqiu, the poor land Sunshu Ao told his son to request so no one would covet it; it is a place allusion, not a "mound of sleep". The literal field has the same error.
At the beginning of Taiqing under Liang, he served as Records Officer of the Western Palace Guard and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
At the beginning of Taiqing under Liang, he served as Records Officer of the Western Palace Guard and concurrently Assistant to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
太常丞 is the Assistant (丞) to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, not the Director of a ministry; the literal field has the same error.
Rui was eloquent in debate. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui greatly valued him and said, "Among all the Yin clan since Jingzhou, none surpasses you."
Rui was eloquent in debate. Minister over the Masses Chu Yanhui greatly valued him and said, "Among all the Yins since the Governor of Jingzhou, none surpasses you."
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the Minister of Works; 荊州 here means Yin Zhongkan, Governor of Jingzhou. The literal field has the same error.
He served under Qi and successively held the post of Attendant of Affairs to the Minister of Works.
He served under Qi and successively held the post of Attendant Gentleman to the Minister over the Masses.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the Minister of Works (司空); the literal field has the same error.
Rui's wife was the daughter of Wang Huan of Langya. Huan was Governor of Yongzhou and recommended Rui as chief clerk of the princely administration.
Rui's wife was the daughter of Wang Huan of Langya. When Huan was Governor of Yongzhou, he recommended Rui as chief clerk of his headquarters.
府長史 is the chief clerk of the governor’s headquarters; Wang Huan was not a prince, so "princely administration" is wrong. The literal field has the same error.
He successively served as Director of the Secretariat and, while in office, memorialized to collate and fix the four divisions of books in the Secret Archive and make a new catalog.
He successively served as Assistant Director of the Palace Library and, while in office, memorialized to collate and fix the four divisions of books in the Secret Archive and make a new catalog.
秘書丞 is the Assistant Director of the Palace Library, not the Director of the Secretariat (中書令); the literal field has the same error.
In the Tianjian era he held the posts of Director of the Palace Library and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
In the Tianjian era he held the posts of Director of the Palace Library and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister over the Masses.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the Minister of Works; the literal field has the same error.
